docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: A flourless banana bread structured by oat flakes: banana and Greek yoghurt bring the moistness, cocoa and cinnamon the flavour. A short bake at 200 °C gives a well-marked crust and a still-fudgy centre. Makes 6 slices. Preparation: 10 minutes. Baking: 30 minutes.

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Rolled oats 50 g Ripe banana 1 Greek yoghurt 150 g Egg 1 Cinnamon 1/2 tsp Unsweetened cocoa powder 20 g Maple syrup 20 g Baking powder 1/2 tsp

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• 1 bowl
  • 1 fork
  • 1 lined loaf tin

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
  2. Mash the banana with a fork, add the egg and yoghurt, mix.
  3. Fold in the oats, cocoa, cinnamon and baking powder, then the maple syrup.
  4. Rest the batter 10 minutes so the flakes hydrate.
  5. Pour into the tin and bake 30 minutes at 200 °C, until a knife blade comes out clean.

docs.title: 5. Key points
docs.text:
• The flakes must be well hydrated before baking, otherwise the centre stays dry.
  • At 200 °C the crust browns fast: check from 25 minutes depending on the tin.
  • A narrow loaf tin gives a dense crumb: a wider tin bakes faster.

docs.title: 6. Variations
docs.text:
• A handful of chocolate chips in the batter.
  • Chopped walnuts for crunch.
  • A banana sliced on top before baking.

docs.title: 7. Serving and storage
docs.text:
• Serve warm or toasted.
  • Storage: 3 days in the fridge.
  • Reheating: 2 minutes in the toaster or 20 seconds in the microwave.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: A tuna brandade gratin: potatoes mashed with milk and butter, mixed with flaked tuna and persillade, gratinated under a golden breadcrumb topping. The potato brings the softness, the tuna the texture, and 15 to 20 minutes in a 180 °C oven binds it all. Serves 4. Preparation: 20 minutes. Cooking: 25 minutes (potatoes) + 20 minutes in the oven.

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Potatoes 1.2 kg Milk 20 cl Butter 40 g Tuna in water (1 large can) 170 g drained Persillade (chopped garlic and parsley) 1 tbsp Mild or Espelette chilli 1 pinch Olive oil 2 tbsp Breadcrumbs 2 tbsp Salt to taste

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• 1 large pot
  • 1 food mill or 1 fork
  • 1 gratin dish

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Peel the potatoes, cut them into chunks and cook 25 minutes in salted water, until a knife blade goes through without resistance. Drain.
  2. Mash the potatoes with a food mill or fork with the hot milk and butter, until you get a soft but not runny purée.
  3. Drain and flake the tuna, fold it into the purée with the persillade, chilli, olive oil and salt. Mix without overworking.
  4. Transfer to the gratin dish, smooth the surface and sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
  5. Bake 15 to 20 minutes at 180 °C, until the surface is golden.

docs.title: 5. Key points
docs.text:
• The brandade should stay soft: add the milk gradually, absorption varies with the potato variety.
  • The tuna is folded in at the end: overworked, it turns pasty.
  • Breadcrumbs mixed with a drizzle of olive oil brown better than dry crumbs.

docs.title: 6. Variations
docs.text:
• A squeeze of lemon juice and the zest of half a lemon in the brandade.
  • Confited cherry tomatoes laid on the surface before gratinating.
  • Replace the tuna with traditional salt cod brandade.

docs.title: 7. Serving and storage
docs.text:
• Serve with a peppery, well-dressed green salad to cut through the softness.
  • Storage: 48 hours in the fridge wrapped in film.
  • Reheating: 15 minutes at 160 °C.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: A fudgy flourless brownie: mashed banana and petits suisses replace butter and flour, cocoa brings the chocolate intensity. Baked in the Cake Factory sharing-cakes programme, 45 minutes. Makes 6 to 8 pieces. Preparation: 15 minutes. Baking: 45 minutes.

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Ripe bananas 4 Eggs 4 Petits suisses (small fresh cheese pots) 4 Unsweetened cocoa powder 30 g Maple syrup 30 to 50 g depending on banana ripeness Baking powder 1 tsp

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• 1 bowl
  • 1 fork or stick blender
  • 1 Cake Factory sharing-cake tin (or a 20 to 22 cm round tin in the oven)

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Mash the bananas with a fork into a smooth purée.
  2. Add the eggs and petits suisses, mix until homogeneous.
  3. Fold in the sifted cocoa and baking powder, then the maple syrup. Mix without overworking.
  4. Pour into the tin and smooth the surface.
  5. Bake 45 minutes in the Cake Factory sharing-cakes programme (or 45 minutes at 180 °C in the oven), until a knife blade comes out barely moist.

docs.title: 5. Key points
docs.text:
• The riper the bananas, the less maple syrup is needed: start with 30 g.
  • The brownie keeps setting as it cools: the centre can stay slightly soft out of the oven.
  • Without flour, the texture is dense and fudgy, not crackly like a classic brownie.

docs.title: 6. Variations
docs.text:
• A handful of dark chocolate chips in the batter.
  • Chopped walnuts or hazelnuts scattered on top before baking.
  • 1 tsp instant coffee dissolved in the batter to deepen the cocoa.

docs.title: 7. Serving and storage
docs.text:
• Serve warm or at room temperature.
  • Storage: 4 days in the fridge wrapped in film.
  • Freezes well in portions, thaw at room temperature.

docs.title: Caghuse (pork, onion and prune pot roast)
1. Overview
docs.text: Caghuse is a slow-braised pork leg roast with onions and prunes, built on cider vinegar and baked in an oven started cold. The vinegar's acidity and the prunes' sweetness balance the softness of the confit onions, and the gentle oven cooking makes the roast meltingly tender. Serves 6. Preparation: 25 minutes. Cooking: 1 hour.

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Pork leg roast (rouelle) 1.2 kg Large onions 6 Potatoes 1 kg Butter 100 g Cider vinegar 15 cl Cider 15 cl Prunes 150 g Bay leaves 2 Salt, pepper to taste

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• 1 cast iron Dutch oven with lid, oven-safe
  • 1 board and 1 knife
  • 1 small saucepan for the vinegar

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Peel and quarter the onions.
  2. Place two thirds of the onions at the bottom of the pot with the butter. Cover with the whole roast. Brown the roast with the onions 10 minutes over medium heat, season with salt and pepper.
  3. Meanwhile, peel the potatoes and cut them into chunks.
  4. Cover the roast with the remaining third of onions and the potatoes.
  5. Bring the vinegar to the boil in a saucepan, then pour the vinegar and the cider into the pot.
  6. Season again with salt and pepper. Add the prunes and bay leaves.
  7. Cover and put in a cold oven, 1 hour at 190 °C. If time allows, baste regularly, turning the roast and the onions.

docs.title: 5. Key points
docs.text:
• The oven starts cold: the gradual rise in temperature avoids thermal shock on the cast iron and lets the meat relax.
  • Vinegar boiled before adding loses its harshness: do not pour it in cold.
  • Rest the roast 10 minutes before slicing: the juices redistribute through the meat.

docs.title: 6. Variations
docs.text:
• Pork chops or shoulder instead of the leg roast, extending the cooking by 15 minutes.
  • Two apples quartered and added with the prunes.
  • A glass of calvados flambed over the meat before putting it in the oven.

docs.title: 7. Serving and storage
docs.text:
• Serve straight from the pot, with the potatoes and onions.
  • Storage: 2 to 3 days in the fridge; freezes well without the potatoes.
  • Reheating: 20 minutes at 150 °C, covered, with a splash of cider.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: Shallots slowly melted in butter then deglazed with white wine, this compote accompanies pan-seared scallops, pan-fried white fish or grilled meat. The wine reduction brings the acidity that lifts mild products. Quantity for 2 people, as an accompaniment to 8 to 10 scallops. Preparation: 10 minutes. Cooking: 30 minutes.

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Shallots 8 Unsalted butter 30 g Dry white wine 10 cl Flat parsley a few sprigs Salt, pepper to taste

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• 1 heavy-bottomed saucepan
  • 1 paring knife

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Finely slice the shallots.
  2. Melt them 15 to 20 minutes over low heat in the butter with a pinch of salt, without colouring. The shallots should turn translucent, pearly and melting.
  3. Deglaze with the white wine, scraping the bottom of the pan to release the juices.
  4. Reduce over low heat for about 10 minutes, until almost no liquid remains. The compote is ready when it looks glossy and slightly syrupy, with no water at the bottom.
  5. Off the heat, season with salt and pepper. The seasoning should be assertive: the compote lifts very mild accompaniments.
  6. Keep off the heat. Chopped parsley goes in at the last moment, never during cooking or storage: cooked or stored, it darkens and loses its flavour.

docs.title: 5. Reuse and reheating
docs.text:
• Storage: one night in the fridge in a closed container, without parsley.
  • Reheating: very low heat, 5 to 8 minutes covered, with 2 to 3 tbsp of water or a splash of white wine to loosen the texture.
  • Finishing touch when serving: a knob of butter swirled in off the heat, for gloss and smoothness. Cream is not recommended: it masks the fruitiness of the reduction and weighs the side dish down.

docs.title: 6. Plating with scallops
docs.text:
1. Pat the scallops dry, season with salt and pepper. Take them out of the fridge 15 minutes before cooking.
  2. Sear 1 minute per side in foaming butter, no longer: the centre must stay pearly.
  3. Plate a spoonful of warm compote, set the scallops on top, scatter with chopped parsley and fleur de sel.

docs.title: 7. Tips
docs.text:
• A slightly rubbery texture after reduction is fixed when reheating: cooking covered over low heat with a little water softens the shallots in a few minutes.
  • The compote freezes very well for up to 3 months.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: A short-cooking fruit jam set with agar agar: the gel forms while cooling, without a long reduction, which keeps the fresh fruit taste. Inverting the jars after filling pasteurises the surface and the lid. Makes three 250 g jars. Preparation: 15 minutes. Cooking: 20 minutes.

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Fruit (fresh or frozen) 1 kg Water 300 ml Agave syrup or maple syrup 100 g Agar agar 2 g

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• 1 large saucepan
  • 1 skimmer
  • 3 x 250 g jars with lids

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Wash, prepare and cut the fruit into pieces.
  2. Heat the fruit with the water in the saucepan over medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes, until the fruit has completely broken down.
  3. Rain in the agar agar and boil 2 minutes, stirring: agar agar only gels after boiling.
  4. Off the heat, add the agave syrup and stir.
  5. Pour straight into the jars and close.
  6. Wait 15 minutes.
  7. Turn the jars upside down and let them cool at room temperature.

docs.title: 5. Key points
docs.text:
• The agar agar must be brought to the boil to activate, otherwise the jam will not set.
  • The jam stays liquid while hot: it sets as it cools, and firms up in the fridge.
  • Inverting the jars sterilises the lid and the surface: do not skip it.
  • With little sugar, the shelf life is shorter than a classic jam.

docs.title: 6. Variations
docs.text:
• Blend half the fruit for a smoother jam.
  • A vanilla pod or the zest of half a lemon cooked with the fruit.
  • A mix of red berries, or apricot and peach in summer.

docs.title: 7. Serving and storage
docs.text:
• Open the jars only once completely cooled.
  • Opened jars: 1 to 2 weeks in the fridge.
  • Unopened jars: 3 to 4 weeks in the fridge, or in a cool dark place otherwise.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: A croque monsieur topped with a comté and old-style mustard béchamel. The béchamel keeps the bread moist during storage, so the croque monsieur stays soft when reheated. Makes 2 meal boxes. Preparation: 30 minutes. Cooking: 15 minutes.

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Crustless (or brioche) sandwich bread 8 slices White ham 160 g Grated comté and emmental (mix) 120 g Butter 40 g Flour 2 tbsp Whole milk 25 cl Old-style (grain) mustard 1 tsp Nutmeg 1 pinch Salt, pepper to taste

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• 1 saucepan
  • 1 lidded frying pan
  • 1 whisk
  • 2 glass meal boxes

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Béchamel: melt 20 g of butter in the saucepan over medium heat, add the flour and stir for 1 minute to make a roux. Pour in the hot milk gradually, whisking. Add 1 tbsp of grated cheese, the mustard, nutmeg, salt and pepper. Leave to thicken 3 to 4 minutes over low heat.
  2. Spread a thin layer of béchamel on 4 slices of bread. Place 1 slice of ham and 20 g of grated cheese on each, then close with the remaining slices.
  3. Coat the top with a second layer of béchamel and sprinkle with grated cheese.
  4. Melt the remaining butter in the pan over medium heat. Cook the croque monsieurs 4 to 5 minutes per side, covered so the cheese melts. Oven option: 10 minutes at 180 °C after brushing with melted butter.

docs.title: 5. Serving and storage
docs.text:
• Reheating: 2 minutes in the microwave at full power, or 5 minutes in the oven at 160 °C to bring the crunch back.
  • Storage: up to 3 days in the fridge. The croque monsieurs can also be assembled and stored raw, then cooked the same day.

docs.title: 6. Variations
docs.text:
• Add pan-fried sliced mushrooms to the béchamel.
  • Replace the comté with gruyère or cheddar.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: A dhal of red lentils and melting potatoes, bound with coconut milk. The crushed tomatoes bring acidity and the lemon juice, added at the end, lifts the roundness of the coconut. A complete vegetarian one-pot dish. Makes 5 portions. Preparation: 15 minutes. Cooking: 30 minutes.

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Olive oil 15 ml (1 tbsp) Cumin seeds 1 tsp Onion 1 Garlic 3 cloves Grated fresh ginger 1 tsp Curry powder 2 tsp Crushed tomatoes (1 can) 400 g Potatoes 800 g Chicken stock 700 ml Red lentils 200 g Coconut milk 400 ml Lemons 3 (juice) Fresh coriander (cilantro) a few sprigs Salt, pepper to taste

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• 1 large Dutch oven or stockpot
  • 1 board and 1 knife
  • 1 fine grater for the ginger

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Heat the oil in the pot over medium heat. Cook the sliced onion and cumin seeds for 3 minutes, without colouring.
  2. Add the chopped garlic and grated ginger, cook 1 minute, then the curry powder for 30 seconds, stirring.
  3. Pour in the crushed tomatoes, stir, then add the potatoes in 2 cm chunks and the stock.
  4. Bring to the boil, lower the heat and simmer 12 to 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
  5. Add the red lentils and coconut milk, cook 10 to 12 minutes over low heat, stirring regularly, until the lentils have melted and thickened the dhal.
  6. Off the heat, add the lemon juice, salt and pepper. Adjust the seasoning.
  7. Scatter chopped coriander over when serving.

docs.title: 5. Key points
docs.text:
• Red lentils catch on the bottom at the end of cooking: stir regularly for the last 10 minutes.
  • The lemon juice goes in off the boil: its aroma evaporates if cooked.
  • The dhal thickens a lot as it rests: keep some hot water for reheating.

docs.title: 6. Variations
docs.text:
• A handful of fresh spinach stirred in at the end of cooking.
  • A fresh chilli chopped with the garlic for a spicier dhal.
  • Sweet potatoes instead of potatoes.

docs.title: 7. Serving and storage
docs.text:
• Serve with basmati rice or naan bread, scattered with coriander.
  • Storage: 4 days in the fridge in an airtight container.
  • Reheating: over low heat with a splash of water, 5 minutes.
  • Freezes well for up to 3 months.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
A frittata with melting potatoes and chopped spring onions (scallions), cooked in a pan then browned under the grill. Pre-cooking the potatoes in water or steam guarantees a melting texture without extending the pan cooking time.

Serves 4 — Preparation: 15 min — Cooking: 10 min (potatoes) + 15 min in the pan and under the grill

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Potatoes 600 g Spring onions (scallions), greens included 4 Eggs 6 Grated parmesan (optional) 2 tbsp Olive oil 2 tbsp Salt, pepper to taste

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• Oven-safe frying pan (removable or metal handle)
  • Large pot or steamer for the pre-cooking
  • Bowl and fork to beat the eggs
  • Platter or serving board for unmoulding

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Peel the potatoes and cut them into roughly 5 mm slices. Cook 10 min in salted boiling water or steam, until tender but still firm. Drain.
  2. Slice the spring onions, whites and greens separately.
  3. Beat the eggs in a bowl with the parmesan, salt and pepper.
  4. Heat the olive oil in the pan over medium heat. Fry the potatoes and the white parts of the spring onions 8 to 10 min, stirring regularly, until lightly coloured. Add the green tops at the end.
  5. Pour the beaten eggs over the potatoes, spread evenly and cook over low heat, covered, 6 to 8 min until the top is just set.
  6. Slide the pan under the oven grill for 2 to 3 min to brown the surface.
  7. Rest for 2 min, then slide the frittata onto a plate. Serve warm or cold.

docs.title: 5. Variations
docs.text:
• Add grilled bacon bits or shredded ham to the potatoes for a complete version.
  • Fold in sliced peppers fried with the spring onions.
  • Replace the parmesan with crumbled goat cheese, added at the end of the pan cooking.
  • Add a few drops of fresh cream to the beaten eggs for a softer texture.

docs.title: 6. Key points
docs.text:
• A non-stick or well-oiled pan makes unmoulding easy without breaking.
  • Too high a heat browns the bottom before the centre is cooked: keep the heat low after adding the eggs.
  • Watch the time under the grill, the surface browns quickly.
  • The frittata reheats poorly at high temperature: eat it warm or cold, or reheat it gently in the oven at 120 °C.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: Small cheese choux served as an appetizer, the gougère is the savoury version of choux pastry. This comté recipe makes about 30 mini 2 cm gougères, for 4 to 6 people with drinks. Preparation: 25 minutes. Cooking: 15 to 18 minutes.

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Unsalted butter 75 g Water 10 cl Milk 5 cl Salt 1/2 tsp Flour 90 g Eggs 3 (to adjust) Grated comté 100 g Espelette pepper 1 pinch (optional)

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• 1 saucepan
  • 1 wooden spatula
  • 1 bowl
  • 1 baking sheet lined with baking paper
  • 1 piping bag or 2 small spoons

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
  2. Pour the water, milk, diced butter and salt into a saucepan. Bring to the boil: the butter must be completely melted at the first boil.
  3. Off the heat, add all the flour at once and stir vigorously with the spatula.
  4. Return to low heat for 1 minute to dry the dough: it forms a ball that pulls away from the sides.
  5. Transfer to a bowl and let it cool for 2 minutes, so the eggs do not cook on contact.
  6. Beat in the eggs one by one, waiting for each to be absorbed before adding the next. Add the third egg gradually: the dough is ready when it is soft, glossy and forms a ribbon that folds back when you lift the spatula.
  7. Add the grated comté and Espelette pepper, then mix.
  8. PIPE: form 2 cm mounds on the baking sheet, well spaced, with a piping bag or two spoons.

docs.title: 5. Baking
docs.text:
• Bake 15 to 18 minutes at 200 °C, without opening the door during baking.
  • The gougères are done when puffed and golden, and they sound slightly hollow when tapped.

docs.title: 6. Storage and reheating
docs.text:
• Cooled gougères: 24 hours at room temperature in a non-airtight box, or 3 days in the fridge.
  • Reheating: 5 minutes at 150 °C, which restores the day's crispness.
  • Can be frozen once cooked, reheated 8 minutes at 150 °C without thawing.

docs.title: 7. Variations
docs.text:
• Emmental or gruyère instead of comté.
  • A few chopped thyme leaves in the dough.
  • Classic version with 4 to 5 cm gougères: bake 20 to 25 minutes.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: A one-pot dish where the rice cooks directly in a broth flavoured with chorizo, peppers, red beans and corn. The chorizo fat diffuses into the rice while it cooks and keeps the dish moist after several days of storage; basmati rice stays nicely separate when reheated. Makes 3 meal boxes. Preparation: 15 minutes. Cooking: 25 minutes.

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text:
Ingredient Quantity Cooking chorizo, diced 200 g Basmati (or long grain) rice 150 g Diced red pepper 1 Diced yellow pepper 1 Sliced red onion 1 small Canned red kidney beans, drained 240 g Canned corn, drained 150 g Canned crushed tomatoes 200 g Chopped garlic 2 cloves Cumin 1 tsp Smoked paprika 1 tsp Cayenne pepper (optional) 1/2 tsp Chicken stock 40 cl Olive oil 2 tbsp Salt, pepper to taste Fresh coriander (cilantro) for finishing

A cooking chorizo works better than the dry snack-type chorizo, which hardens when cooked. Adjust the stock to the rice: if the grains are still firm after 20 minutes, add 5 cl of hot water and cook 5 more minutes, covered.

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• 1 Dutch oven or stockpot with a lid
  • 3 glass meal boxes

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Cook the onion and garlic in the olive oil over medium heat for 3 minutes, without colouring.
  2. Add the diced chorizo and brown it for 5 minutes so it releases its fat.
  3. Add the peppers, cumin, smoked paprika and cayenne, season with salt and pepper, then cook for 3 minutes.
  4. Stir in the rice and stir for 1 minute to coat it in fat and spices.
  5. Pour in the crushed tomatoes, red beans, corn and stock.
  6. Bring to the boil, lower the heat, cover and simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the rice is cooked and the liquid absorbed.
  7. Cool for 10 minutes, then divide between the 3 glass boxes.

docs.title: 5. Serving and storage
docs.text:
• Reheating: 3 to 4 minutes in the microwave at full power with 1 tbsp of water, stirring halfway, or over low heat in a pan with a splash of water.
  • Fresh coriander survives neither cooking nor storage: keep it separate and scatter it over at mealtime.
  • Storage: 4 to 5 days in the fridge.

docs.title: 6. Variations
docs.text:
• Replace the chorizo with pork strips or prawns, added at the end of cooking.
  • Replace the cayenne with mild paprika for a milder version.
  • Scatter grated cheddar over when reheating.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
A chicken basquaise prepared entirely in a single Dutch oven: the chicken is seared, the vegetables are confited in the cooking juices, with no transfers between several pots. The aromatic base sticks to the traditional trio of tomatoes, peppers and onion, lifted with Espelette pepper. A cast iron pot, which spreads the heat evenly, ensures gentle cooking that binds the sauce without constant watching.

Serves 4 — Preparation: 15 min — Cooking: 45 min

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Chicken thighs 4 Red peppers 2 Green pepper 1 Ripe tomatoes or canned peeled tomatoes 4 (or 400 g) Onion 1 Garlic 2 cloves Olive oil 2 tbsp Espelette pepper 1 tsp Bay leaf 1 Fresh thyme 2 sprigs Tomato concentrate 1 tsp Diced Bayonne ham (optional) 100 g Black olives (optional) 10 Salt, pepper to taste

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• 4 to 5 L cast iron Dutch oven with lid
  • Board and cook's knife
  • Kitchen tongs to turn the thighs

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Seed the peppers and cut them into 1 cm strips. Slice the onion, chop the garlic, dice the tomatoes (keep them whole if canned).
  2. Heat the olive oil in the pot over medium heat. Brown the chicken thighs on each side, 6 to 8 min in total, then set them aside on a plate.
  3. Cook the onion and garlic for 3 min in the pot, without washing it. Add the peppers and Bayonne ham, continue for 5 min until the peppers start to soften.
  4. Add the tomatoes, tomato concentrate, Espelette pepper, bay leaf and thyme. Season with salt and pepper, mix.
  5. Nestle the thighs into the vegetables, skin side up. Cover and simmer over low heat for 30 to 35 min, until the meat comes off the bone with a fork.
  6. Remove the lid for the last 5 minutes to thicken the sauce if it is still runny. Add the olives 5 min before the end of cooking.
  7. Remove the bay leaf and thyme sprigs, adjust the seasoning. Serve straight from the pot.

docs.title: 5. Variations
docs.text:
• Replace the thighs with a farm chicken cut into eight pieces, extending the covered cooking time by 10 min.
  • Add 1 tsp smoked paprika to the Espelette pepper for a woodier profile.
  • Deglaze the pot with dry white wine (10 cl) after cooking the onion, before adding the tomatoes.
  • Scatter chopped flat parsley over just before serving.

docs.title: 6. Key points
docs.text:
• Too high a heat makes the tomatoes stick to the bottom: keep the heat low throughout the simmering.
  • The chicken should be browned, not cooked, at step 2: it cooks through while simmering.
  • Espelette pepper mellows as it cooks: taste the sauce at the end before adding more.
  • Leftovers keep 2 to 3 days in the fridge and gain flavour when reheated, over low heat and covered.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: High-protein pancakes with no added sugar: the banana sweetens the batter naturally, Greek yoghurt brings the moistness and baking powder the lift. The thick batter makes 6 to 8 small pancakes for 2 people. Preparation: 10 minutes. Cooking: 10 minutes.

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Ripe banana 1 Eggs 2 Greek yoghurt 200 g Flour 40 g Baking powder 1/2 tsp

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• 1 bowl
  • 1 fork or stick blender
  • 1 non-stick pan
  • 1 small ladle

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Mash the banana with a fork into a rough purée.
  2. Add the eggs and yoghurt, mix until homogeneous.
  3. Fold in the flour and baking powder without overworking: the batter should stay thick.
  4. Rest the batter 10 minutes so the baking powder starts working.
  5. Heat the pan over medium-low heat, with a thin film of oil if needed.
  6. Drop small ladles of batter, spread slightly, cook 2 to 3 minutes until bubbles form on the surface, flip, then cook 1 to 2 more minutes.

docs.title: 5. Key points
docs.text:
• The batter is thicker than a classic pancake batter: do not try to smooth it completely.
  • Too high a heat browns the surface before the centre cooks: keep the heat medium-low.
  • A very ripe banana sweetens the batter more and caramelises faster.

docs.title: 6. Variations
docs.text:
• 1/2 tsp cinnamon or cocoa in the batter.
  • A few blueberries dropped on each pancake before flipping.
  • Pan-fried banana slices as a topping.

docs.title: 7. Serving and storage
docs.text:
• Serve warm, with a little Greek yoghurt or fresh fruit.
  • Storage: 48 hours in the fridge once cooked.
  • Reheating: 30 seconds in the microwave or a few minutes in the toaster.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: A Polish apple cake: a soft brioche topped with apple slices and a cinnamon crumble, baked in the Cake Factory sharing-cakes programme. The 40 °C proof speeds up the brioche rise and gives a light crumb without a long wait at room temperature. Makes 8 slices. Preparation: 30 minutes. Proofing: 1 h 30. Baking: 45 minutes.

docs.title: Brioche
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Flour 300 g Milk 120 ml Unsalted butter 80 g Sugar 60 g Eggs 2 Fresh yeast 21 g Salt 1/2 tsp

docs.title: Filling
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Apples 3

docs.title: Crumble
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Flour 150 g Sugar 100 g Cold unsalted butter 90 g Cinnamon 1 tsp

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• 1 stand mixer or 1 bowl for kneading by hand
  • 1 round tin or the Cake Factory sharing-cake tin
  • 1 Cake Factory or 1 oven

docs.title: 4. Brioche dough
docs.text:
1. Warm the milk to about 40 °C and dissolve the crumbled fresh yeast in it.
  2. Mix the flour, sugar and salt in the mixer bowl. Add the eggs then the yeasted milk, and knead 10 minutes at medium speed.
  3. Add the diced butter gradually, waiting for each addition to be incorporated. Knead 10 more minutes, until the dough is soft and pulls away from the sides.
  4. Cover and let rise 1 h 30 at 40 °C (oven warmed then switched off, or proofing programme), until the dough has doubled.

docs.title: 5. Crumble and filling
docs.text:
1. Rub the flour, sugar, cinnamon and cold diced butter between your fingertips until sandy. Keep in the fridge.
  2. Core the apples and cut them into thin slices.

docs.title: 6. Assembly and baking
docs.text:
1. Butter the tin and spread the dough about 2 cm thick.
  2. Arrange the apple slices over the dough.
  3. Crumble the topping over the apples in an even layer.
  4. Bake 45 minutes at 180 °C (Cake Factory sharing-cakes programme), until the crumble is golden and the dough baked through.
  5. Cool for 30 minutes before unmoulding.

docs.title: 7. Key points
docs.text:
• Fresh yeast dies above 45 °C: the milk must be warm, never hot.
  • The butter goes in only once the dough is formed: adding it too early gives a greasy, sticky dough.
  • Without a 40 °C proofer, let the dough rise 2 hours at room temperature, away from drafts.
  • An overworked crumble turns greasy: rub quickly and keep the butter cold.

docs.title: 8. Variations
docs.text:
• Pears or apricots in season instead of apples.
  • A few soaked sultanas scattered over the brioche before baking.
  • Replace half the crumble sugar with brown sugar for a more caramelised taste.

docs.title: 9. Serving and storage
docs.text:
• Serve warm or at room temperature.
  • Storage: 3 days under a cake dome at room temperature.
  • Reheating: 5 minutes at 150 °C to restore the crumble's crunch.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
Stuffed potatoes filled with their own flesh mixed with fresh garlic-and-herb cheese (Boursin type), gratinated in the oven. The microwave pre-cooking cuts the preparation time drastically compared to a fully oven-baked version.

Serves 4 — Preparation: 15 min — Cooking: 10 min in the microwave + 15 min in the oven (200 °C)

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Floury potatoes (Russet, Maris Piper) 4 large, even-sized Fresh cheese, Boursin type (shallot & chive) 150 g Butter 1 knob per potato Salt, pepper to taste

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• Microwave oven
  • Conventional oven, grill or fan setting
  • Fork or Parisian scoop for hollowing
  • Bowl and fork for mashing

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Wash the potatoes without peeling them. Prick them all over with a fork.
  2. Pre-cook in the microwave at full power: 8 to 10 min for four potatoes, turning them halfway. They should stay firm.
  3. Let them cool for a few minutes, then cut them in half lengthwise.
  4. Scoop out about half of the flesh of each half with a fork, keeping a wall of about 1 cm.
  5. Mash the scooped-out flesh in a bowl, then mix with the fresh cheese, salt and pepper.
  6. Divide the filling between the potato halves.
  7. Place a knob of butter on each filled half.
  8. Gratinate in the oven at 200 °C, grill setting, for 12 to 15 min until golden.

docs.title: 5. Variations
docs.text:
• Add grilled bacon bits or shredded ham to the filling for a complete version.
  • Replace part of the fresh cheese with grated cheese (comté, gruyère) for a stronger gratin.
  • Chop fresh chives over the potatoes at the end of cooking.

docs.title: 6. Key points
docs.text:
• Even-sized potatoes guarantee uniform cooking.
  • Hollowing out too much weakens the wall: keep about 1 cm of flesh.
  • Watch the gratin at the end of cooking, the grill browns quickly.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: A dish of diced poultry simmered in a coconut milk and fresh cream sauce flavoured with curry, with red pepper and tomato purée. The sauce is smooth, slightly sweet and medium in strength; the pepper brings crunch and colour. Serve it with rice or flatbread for a complete everyday meal. Serves 4, with 15 minutes of preparation and 25 minutes of cooking.

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text:
Ingredient Quantity Chicken or turkey fillets or breasts 700 g Coconut milk 400 ml Thick fresh cream 20 cl Red pepper 1 Tomato purée 2 tbsp Onion 1 Garlic 2 cloves Fresh ginger 20 g (a 2 cm piece) Red or yellow curry paste 2 tbsp Vegetable or coconut oil 1 tbsp Sugar 1 tsp Fresh coriander (cilantro) a few sprigs Salt, pepper to taste

As a substitute for the curry paste: 1 tbsp curry powder and 1 tsp ground cumin. The coconut milk and cream amounts tolerate ±20 % without affecting the texture of the sauce.

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• Heavy-bottomed Dutch oven or deep pan
  • Board and knife
  • Fine grater for the ginger
  • Wooden spoon

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Finely dice the onion and garlic, grate the ginger.
  2. Seed the red pepper and cut it into strips.
  3. Cut the poultry into roughly 3 cm dice, season with salt and pepper.
  4. Heat the oil in the pot over medium heat and brown the poultry dice for 5 minutes, stirring, then set aside.
  5. Cook the onion, garlic and ginger for 3 minutes in the pot, without colouring.
  6. Add the curry paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring.
  7. Add the red pepper and cook for 3 minutes.
  8. Add the tomato purée and stir for 1 minute.
  9. Pour in the coconut milk, scraping the juices from the bottom of the pot.
  10. Return the poultry, add the sugar, then simmer 12 to 15 minutes over low heat, covered.
  11. Stir in the fresh cream and cook 5 more minutes over low heat.
  12. Adjust the seasoning with salt, pepper and sugar.
  13. Scatter chopped coriander over just before serving.

docs.title: 5. Serving and storage
docs.text:
• Serve with basmati or Thai rice, or flatbread such as naan.
  • The coriander goes in at the very last moment, off the heat.
  • Can be eaten straight away or later.
  • Storage: 3 days in the fridge in an airtight container.
  • Reheating: 5 to 7 minutes over low heat stirring, or 2 minutes in the microwave at medium power.
  • Freezing not recommended: the fresh cream may split when thawing.

docs.title: 6. Variations
docs.text:
• Replace the fresh cream with Greek yoghurt → lighter version, stirred in off the heat.
  • Add 1 tbsp peanut butter at step 9 → thicker sauce with a nutty taste.
  • Add 1 finely chopped fresh chilli with the pepper → spicier dish.
  • Replace the poultry with prawns → cook only 5 minutes after adding the coconut milk.
  • Cook the rice in half coconut milk, half water → fragrant side dish.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: A poultry sauté in cider: the floured pieces give body to the sauce, the cider brings acidity, and the melting apples the sweetness that balances the dish. Cream is stirred in at the end to soften it. Serves 4. Preparation: 15 minutes. Cooking: 25 minutes.

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Chicken or turkey breasts 800 g Flour 2 tbsp Butter 30 g Onion 1 Apples 3 Dry cider 25 to 30 cl Thick cream 10 cl Thyme 2 sprigs Salt, pepper to taste

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• 1 lidded deep pan
  • 1 board and 1 knife

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Slice the onion. Core the apples and cut them into quarters, without peeling.
  2. Cut the poultry into pieces, season with salt and pepper, and dust with flour.
  3. Melt the butter in the pan over medium heat and brown the poultry for 5 minutes, stirring, then set aside.
  4. Cook the onion 3 minutes without colouring, add the apples and thyme, cook 5 minutes.
  5. Deglaze with the cider, scraping the juices from the bottom. Return the poultry, cover and simmer 10 to 12 minutes over low heat, until the apples are melting.
  6. Stir in the cream and cook 2 more minutes over low heat. Adjust the seasoning.

docs.title: 5. Key points
docs.text:
• The flour coats the poultry and naturally thickens the sauce: do not skip it.
  • The apples break down if cooked too long: keep them in firm quarters, or crush them with a fork for a stewed-apple sauce.
  • The cider reduces and loses its bitterness while cooking: taste the sauce before salting at the end.

docs.title: 6. Variations
docs.text:
• 1 tbsp calvados added with the cider.
  • A few smoked bacon bits fried with the onion.
  • Steamed potatoes or rice on the side.

docs.title: 7. Serving and storage
docs.text:
• Serve with rice, mash or steamed potatoes.
  • Storage: 3 days in the fridge in an airtight container.
  • Reheating: 5 to 7 minutes over low heat, without boiling or the cream will split.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: A shortcrust pastry tart filled with almond frangipane and thinly sliced pears arranged in a rosette. A festive dessert, served warm or at room temperature, optionally dusted with icing sugar. 22 to 24 cm tin, makes 6 to 8 slices. Preparation: 40 minutes. Baking: 40 to 45 minutes. The pastry and frangipane can both be made the day before without any loss of quality.

docs.title: Shortcrust pastry
docs.text:
Ingredient Quantity Flour 200 g Cold unsalted butter 100 g Egg 1 Sugar 1 pinch Salt 1 pinch

A store-bought pure butter shortcrust pastry works as a replacement.

docs.title: Frangipane
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Ground almonds 100 g Soft unsalted butter 80 g Sugar 80 g Eggs 2 Bitter almond extract or rum 1 tsp or 1 tbsp (optional)

docs.title: Topping and finishing
docs.text: Ingredient Quantity Ripe pears (Conference type) 4 Icing sugar to taste

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• 1 tart tin, 22 to 24 cm
  • 1 whisk or spatula
  • 1 fork
  • 1 paring knife

docs.title: 4. Shortcrust pastry
docs.text:
1. Rub the flour, cold diced butter, salt and sugar between your fingertips until the mixture is sandy.
  2. Add the egg and bring together into a ball without overworking the dough.
  3. Smear the dough once or twice with the palm of your hand, shape it into a disc, wrap in film.
  4. Rest in the fridge for at least 30 minutes, ideally overnight.

docs.title: 5. Frangipane
docs.text:
1. Cream the soft butter and sugar until homogeneous.
  2. Add the ground almonds, then the eggs one by one.
  3. Flavour with bitter almond extract or rum.
  4. The frangipane keeps overnight in the fridge in a closed container.

docs.title: 6. Assembly
docs.text:
1. Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F).
  2. Line the tin with the pastry and prick the base with a fork.
  3. Spread the frangipane over the pastry base.
  4. Peel the pears, slice them thinly and remove the core.
  5. Arrange the slices in a rosette over the frangipane, pressing them in lightly.

docs.title: 7. Baking
docs.text:
1. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes at 180 °C (350 °F).
  2. The tart is done when the frangipane is puffed and golden and the pastry is cooked underneath.
  3. Let it cool on a rack for at least 1 hour: the frangipane sets and the tart cuts cleanly.

docs.title: 8. Serving and storage
docs.text:
• Serve warm or at room temperature, dusted with icing sugar.
  • Storage: 48 hours at room temperature under a cake dome, 4 days in the fridge.
  • Optional reheating: 10 minutes at 150 °C (300 °F).

docs.title: 9. Variations
docs.text:
• Pears poached for 10 minutes in a light syrup, for extra softness.
  • Fresh apricots in season instead of pears.
  • A few flaked almonds scattered on top before baking.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: A thick, smooth soup with a coating texture, served in small glasses as an appetizer or as a starter. The butternut squash brings the melt-in-the-mouth body, the coconut milk the roundness. Makes 4 small glasses or 2 bowls. Preparation: 10 minutes. Cooking: 25 minutes.

docs.title: 2. Ingredients
docs.text:
Ingredient Quantity Butternut squash flesh, diced 700 g (net weight, peeled and seeded) Yellow onion 1 Coconut milk 20 cl Vegetable stock 50 cl (1 dissolved stock cube) Olive oil 1 tbsp Hazelnuts 2 tbsp Curry powder 1 pinch (optional) Salt, pepper to taste

The 700 g weight is net flesh, after peeling and seeding. A range of 550 to 800 g is fine: the stock is always adjusted to just cover, and the coconut milk never exceeds 20 cl for 700 g of flesh.

docs.title: 3. Equipment
docs.text:
• 1 pot or stockpot
  • 1 stick blender
  • 1 peeler

docs.title: 4. Preparation
docs.text:
1. Slice the onion. Cook it 2 to 3 minutes in the olive oil over medium heat, without colouring.
  2. Peel the squash, remove the seeds and cut the flesh into 2 cm dice.
  3. Add the dice to the pot, stir for 1 minute to coat.
  4. Pour in hot stock to just cover: the liquid should just reach the top of the dice without covering them completely, otherwise the velouté stays runny.
  5. Cover and cook 20 minutes over medium heat, checking halfway that nothing is sticking.
  6. Test the cooking: a knife blade goes through the dice without resistance.
  7. Blend with the coconut milk, salt, pepper and curry. The texture should coat: the velouté holds on the back of a spoon.

docs.title: 5. Serving
docs.text:
• Reheat over low heat before serving, without boiling.
  • Toast the hazelnuts 5 minutes in the oven at 180 °C, crush them and scatter over just before serving.

docs.title: 6. Storage
docs.text:
• 48 hours in the fridge in a closed container.
  • Freezes well for up to 3 months, without the hazelnuts.

docs.title: 7. Variations
docs.text:
• A pinch of ground ginger for a lift.
  • A few drops of hazelnut oil when serving.
  • Replace the butternut with a small Hokkaido pumpkin, no peeling needed.
